report.speaker: Joshua Zahl
report.title: A Survey of the Kakeya Conjecture, 2000–2025
report.question: 丰富方向的线段为何必须占据满维空间，多尺度非集中又如何控制其重叠？
report.reading_scope: Read published §§1–4, including definitions, historical examples, three-dimensional proof outline, broad and narrow estimates; cross-checked arXiv v1. Reused existing projection and restriction branches rather than duplicating them.

proof_scope.2I0C: D(1), exponent convergence and the final volume implication proved; the two geometric improvement propositions are cited.
proof_scope.2I0J: Weighted transversality imposed only on a measurable region carrying a fixed positive fraction of the tube mass. The restricted Lq and Holder deduction is proved; the weighted multilinear input is cited.
proof_scope.2I0K: Full theorem cited; the disjoint counting model only explains the exponent.
proof_scope.2I07: Exact cardinality and containment proved over the dual-number ring; no plane nonconcentration theorem claimed.

deferred: Complete proof of the Wang–Zahl structure and strict-improvement propositions.
Full Bourgain discretized projection theorem and regulus-strip incidence arguments.
Endpoint multilinear Kakeya proof and polynomial partitioning broad/narrow induction.
Complete passage from shaded multiscale estimates to Hausdorff dimension; existing theorem retained with citation.

source_errata: Both publisher and arXiv Conjecture 1.3-prime print an upper bound; 2I03 proves the intended lower-bound direction independently.
Publisher/arXiv shaded variants repeat union T instead of union Y(T). Local statements use the actual shaded union.
The published multilinear sums mix k and n indices. 2I0J consistently sums k-tuples and multiplies k indicators.
The narrow-case heuristic prints mu^(-2); the count delta^(-1)mu^2 times tube volume delta^3 yields delta^2mu^2, as checked in 2I0K.
Source fine-child count (delta/rho)^2 is reversed in one explanatory sentence; no such count is copied into the definition.
